title: Claude Opus 4.8
content:
## Overview

Claude Opus 4.8 (`claude-opus-4-8`) is Anthropic's most capable generally available model, released May 28, 2026. It succeeds Opus 4.7 (April 2026) with a focus on agentic coding reliability, dynamic multi-agent workflows, and expanded context. Pricing is unchanged from Opus 4.7: **$5 per million input tokens and $25 per million output tokens**.

---

## Key Specifications

| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| Model ID | `claude-opus-4-8` |
| Context window | 1M tokens (200K on Microsoft Foundry) |
| Max output tokens | 128K |
| Availability | Claude API, Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud Vertex AI, Microsoft Foundry |
| Price (input) | $5 / 1M tokens |
| Price (output) | $25 / 1M tokens |

---

## Benchmark Performance

Opus 4.8 improves on Opus 4.7 across every tracked benchmark:

| Benchmark | Opus 4.8 | Opus 4.7 | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| SWE-bench Verified | 88.6% | 87.6% | Real-world software engineering tasks |
| SWE-bench Pro | 69.2% | 64.3% | Harder subset; +7.6 points |
| MCP-Atlas | 82.2% | 77.3% | Multi-step tool-use evaluation |
| BrowseComp | 84.3% | 79.3% | Web browsing and comprehension |
| Multidisciplinary reasoning (with tools) | 57.9% | 54.7% | |
| Agentic computer use | 83.4% | 82.8% | |
| Knowledge work score | 1890 | 1753 | Composite score |

On agentic coding (SWE-bench Pro), Opus 4.8 scores 69.2% vs GPT-5.5 at 58.6% — a 10.6-point lead. The 7.6-point improvement on SWE-bench Pro over Opus 4.7 arrived in 41 days; gains of that magnitude previously took 6–12 months between model generations.

---

## Dynamic Workflows

Opus 4.8 ships alongside a **dynamic workflows** capability in Claude Code and the Managed Agents platform. When a task is too large or complex for a single agent pass, Claude can autonomously:

1. Decompose the task into parallelizable subtasks
2. Spin up specialist subagents, each with its own model, prompt, and tool set
3. Execute subtasks concurrently on a shared filesystem
4. Merge and verify results through an orchestrator

This is distinct from manually-defined subagent topologies: the model decides the decomposition at runtime based on task analysis.

---

## Effort Control

Claude.ai users can now explicitly control how much effort Claude applies to a task. Lowering effort reduces latency when a thorough analysis isn't needed; raising it directs Claude to reason more carefully before responding.

---

## Code Reliability

Opus 4.8 is **4× less likely than Opus 4.7** to miss flaws in code it produces. It is also less prone to unsupported factual claims. Combined with dynamic workflows, this makes Opus 4.8 substantially more reliable for autonomous, long-horizon coding tasks.

---

## Fast Mode

Fast mode for Opus 4.8 — which runs the model at approximately 2.5× normal output speed — is now **3× cheaper** than Fast mode was for Opus 4.7. In Claude Code, `/fast` toggles this mode.

---

## Mid-Conversation System Messages

Opus 4.8 introduces support for mid-conversation system messages: you can include `role: "system"` entries after a user turn in the messages array (subject to placement rules). This preserves prompt cache hits when instructions change partway through a long-running session — previously, updating instructions required modifying the conversation prefix and losing cached computation.

---

## What's Next: Mythos Preview

Anthropic separately previewed a **Mythos-class model** in April 2026 — a full capability tier above Opus 4.8, currently restricted to the invitation-only Project Glasswing partner program. Anthropic has confirmed Mythos-class models will reach general customers in the coming weeks.
